reader.requirement: In an ALPHABET literal phrase at --std 85, a numeric literal must be an unsigned integer from 1 through the native character set size (implementor: 65,536), and a nonnumeric literal written with THROUGH or ALSO (either side) must be one character; a multi-character nonnumeric literal without THRU/ALSO stays legal.

edition-consulted.switches: hexadecimal X".." and national N".." literal operands are refused below 2002 (COBOL0900)
the FOR ALPHANUMERIC/NATIONAL phrase is refused below 2002
DialectLevel < 2002 returns early for the LOCALE phrase (not this rule's literal phrase)

reader.edition-search: grep DialectLevel/Edition./ConstructRegistry in SpecialNamesBinder*.cs and CollatingModel.cs: the literal-phrase decoder and the ordinal/length checks never consult the edition; only operand-form gates (hex/national literal, FOR phrase) do.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: the ordinal range and one-character checks are one arm; only later-edition operand forms (X/N literals, FOR NATIONAL, constant-names) are refused at 85
reader.witnesses-cover: part: witnesses cover the at-bound count and the ordinal repertoire; they do not exercise signed, zero, over-bound or non-integer numerics, nor the multi-character THRU/ALSO refusal

probes.printed: COBOL1906 the ordinal 0 does not exist in the native alphanumeric character set (65536 characters)
probes.expected: refused: value within one through the maximum

probes.printed: COBOL1906 the ordinal 65537 does not exist
COBOL1906 the ordinal 123456789012345678 does not exist
COBOL1906 +5 each numeric literal shall be an UNSIGNED integer
COBOL1906 1.5 each noninteger literal shall be an alphanumeric literal
probes.expected: refused: numeric must be an integer

probes.printed: COBOL1906 the operand 'AB' is 2 characters (ALL "AB" THRU "C")
probes.expected: refused: a figurative ALL literal of two characters under THRU
legal: "B" ALSO SPACE share a position, QUOTE THRU "#" one-character figuratives
legal: "ABC" without THRU/ALSO, 65536 at the bound
67 THROUGH 66 = B,A; "ZY" successive; 49 ALSO 50 = '0','1' one position; C unspecified after (GR4d 1-6)

probes.printed: COBOL0900 the hexadecimal alphanumeric literal X"..." requires COBOL-2002
COBOL0900 the national literal N"..." requires COBOL-2002 (plus COBOL1906 class)

OK  §1985:VI.4.5.3 SR4b  (4.5.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR4b

reader.notes: Both items are enforced on one edition-blind path; the run-time collating order built from numeric ordinals and multi-character literals matches GR4d. The diagnostics cite §2023:12.3.7.3 SR14 at --std 85 (wording only, not a conformance fault).
reader.at-2023: same COBOL1906 refusals (sr4_thrulong at 2023 printed the same line)

refuter.evidence: Read §1985:VI.4.5.3 SR4a/SR4b and GR4d 1-6. Probes under refute-1985-050 at --std 85 aimed at literal-2/literal-3 (the reader tested mostly literal-1): r4_also_zero ("A" ALSO 0) COBOL1906 ordinal 0; r4_also_over (ALSO 70000) and r4_thru_over (THRU 70000) COBOL1906 out of range; r4_thru_signed (THRU +70) COBOL1906 UNSIGNED; r4_also3 ("A" ALSO "B" ALSO "CD") COBOL1906 'CD' 2 characters; r4_also_lit1 ("AB" ALSO "C") COBOL1906 'AB'; r4_empty_thru ("" THRU "C") COBOL1906 zero-length plus COBOL0900 zero-length literal requires 2014 (class c); r4_float (1.0E2) COBOL1906 plus COBOL0900 floating literal requires 2002 (class c); r4_quote_thru ("#" THRU """", a one-character literal written with a doubled quote) accepted and ran H-LT-Q=Y Q-LT-A=Y (descending range honored); r4_lead0 (00068 THROUGH 0067 "Z" ALSO 0090) ran C-LT-B=Y B-LT-Z=Y Z-EQ-Y=Y Y-LT-A=Y (leading-zero unsigned integers legal, ordinals right). cite.py: OK §1985:VI.4.5.3 SR4a; OK §1985:VI.4.5.3 SR4b; OK §1985:VI.4.5.4 GR4d.
